Subject: [SmartAssist] sudden throughput drop + token latency spike

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a big impact on our Gen API calls around 08:50 PT this morning — throughput dropped ~40% and p95 token time jumped from ~220ms to ~980ms for a subset of request patterns. Errors are low (5xx ~0.5%) but users are reporting timeouts and partial outputs.

Attached is a short sample of request IDs and request payloads we captured (raw-requests-sample.json). We're on the 2x reserved plan and this is affecting our core chat flows during peak. Can Redwood confirm if there's a system-wide change or if this looks routed to our tenancy?

Please escalate — we need an ETA and a recommended mitigation (can we route to a backup variant or roll to a lower-context model?)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: [SmartAssist] sudden throughput drop + token latency spike

Quick triage notes (SRE):
- We can reproduce the p95 jump for the request fingerprints Alex provided. Primary signal: sustained KV cache churn on the model shard serving SmartAssist's reserved pool starting ~08:45 PT. Eviction rates spiked due to an uneven prefix distribution (heavy long-context requests).
- No evidence of infra node failures; CPU/GPU utilization looks normal but kernel queue depth increased and async batching latencies climbed.

Immediate mitigations we can do (30-90m):
1) Route SmartAssist traffic to the compatible reduced-context variant (same weights, lower max seq) — should reduce KV pressure and restore throughput. Requires a control-plane policy flip; low-risk for quality but expect marginally shorter completions.
2) Temporary burst capacity increase for their reserved pool (if customer agrees) — will increase cost but helps throughput while we stabilize.
3) Apply a transient adaptive batching cap to limit largest batches — reduces tail but may increase per-token cost.

Requesting: a) customer approval for option 1 (routing to reduced-context variant) or option 2 (burst); b) request IDs/time range to correlate logs (we have the samples but need full list). I'll start a canary rollout if we get approval.

Attaching preliminary chart (p95_spike_graph.png) and will open JIRA-9812 to track the long-term fix (root cause: prefix skew + KV eviction heuristics).

Marissa
SRE Lead — Inference Platform
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks for the fast triage, Marissa. A couple of product/roadmap items to call out:
- Short-term routing to a reduced-context variant is an acceptable mitigation, but we should document expected quality delta and have a clear rollback trigger (p95 < 350ms for 30m).
- Long-term fix: JIRA-9812 should include improved KV retention heuristics and a targeted kernel scheduling tweak. If that kernel tweak is required, estimate is non-trivial (Q3 work).

For the customer communication we should propose:
1) Immediate: flip to reduced-context variant now (opt-in) — provide expected p95 improvement and quality note.
2) Near-term: enable 2-hour burst (if they accept cost) while we monitor canary.
3) Roadmap: commit to a post-mortem and a timeline for the KV heuristics change (JIRA-9812).

I'll attach a short mitigation playbook for the CS note you can send — please review and edit.

1) Flip SmartAssist traffic to the reduced-context compatible model variant now (expected p95 improvement from ~980ms -> ~280-340ms for affected fingerprints). This is low-risk for functionality; some completions may be slightly shorter.
2) Enable a 2-hour burst on your reserved pool while we monitor the canary (we will invoice for burst usage per your contract if you accept).

Customer-facing note (draft):
"We observed increased token-level latency and a throughput reduction impacting a subset of requests this morning. If you prefer not to accept the burst cost we can proceed with routing-only.

We appreciate your patience — please confirm which option you prefer and we will proceed immediately.
"
